title: Posted a positive review of Moulin Rouge with Megan Thee Stallion
transcript: Okay, so Megan Thee Stallion fans are very mad at me for saying that she can't sing. And even though for the rest of that video, I went on to praise her performance and say that I had a really good time, I do want to elaborate, because me saying that she can't sing is not the diss that some of y'all are making it out to be. Because when I say singer, I don't mean that she doesn't have any musical talent. She's an incredible performer and rapper. But that's very different from singing, which requires a completely different technique. And one of the things that Megan and the team at Moulin Rouge, I think, did really well is they understood where her strengths lied, and they tailored the role to those strengths. And so, yes, that meant removing the parts of the score that required her to belt, because that is not necessarily something that is in her wheelhouse. But it's also not a critical part of making this role work. To be a good Zidler, you just have to be a good showman. Or showwoman in this case. And Megan Thee Stallion has that in spades. The vocals aren't nearly as important as a role like Satine or Christian. And so you can get away with casting someone who does not have the singing capabilities of a standard Broadway performer and is able to fall back on things like their stage presence and their comedic timing In Order to make the role work. That's really all I was trying to say. And if you are a Megan fan, it's okay to admit that she is not the strongest singer. No one is perfect at everything. And that is okay. It does not make her any less talented.
reasoning: The reviewer praises Megan Thee Stallion's performance despite vocal limitations, highlighting her strengths as a performer and the smart casting/adaptation decisions. The overall tone is appreciative and recommending.
